title.value: Exploring trust development in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers: A scoping review of the literature
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus of the paper, which is an exploration of trust development in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers.
title.quote: Exploring trust development in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers: A scoping review of the literature

extractions.description: This paper reviews literature on trust development in pediatric surgical and emergency care settings. It identifies factors fostering trust, gaps in research, and areas for improvement in patient-physician relationships within these specific contexts. The study highlights constructs such as competence, communication, dependability, and caring, with an emphasis on communication and compassionate care to enhance trust.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The focus of the paper is on trust development in pediatric medical settings, which is not directly related to climate or ecologically-related sustainable development. It primarily deals with social aspects of healthcare.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Trust is central to the therapeutic relationship between patients and their providers, yet little is known about how it is developed in the unique context of children facing surgical emergencies.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not relate to any identified Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories. It focuses on trust dynamics in healthcare, specifically in pediatric surgical and emergency care.
primary_category.quote: We sought to identify factors fostering trust development, gaps, and areas for improvement.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper does not align with any primary Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development category, no specific sub-category is relevant.
primary_sub_category.quote: Out of 5578 articles screened, 12 fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Four major trust constructs were identified: competence, communication, dependability, and caring.

new_primary_category.justification: The subject matter of this paper is not directly applicable to the pre-defined Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: Improving communication and providing compassionate care, as well as encouraging a patient-centered approach, appear to be most effective in promoting trust in pediatric surgical and urgent settings.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new category as the paper does not cover Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development topics.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings can guide future educational interventions towards strengthening parental trust and promoting child- and family-centered care in pediatric surgical settings.
